T-INDEX.note: Concept B, The Standing Index. Owner picked it on 2026-08-21 from a 3-concept tournament (a/b/c on disk), all three laying out the FINAL copy of blog unedited. THE PROBLEM THIS TYPE POSES: all four T-INDEX pages (blog, category-events, media, store) ship with ZERO items and an explicitly flagged empty state, and the copy forbids invented posts, stock feeds, fabricated authors, dates or outlets. So the design question was how a page whose subject is its own absence avoids looking broken. B answers it by making the READINESS the subject rather than the absence: a full-width masthead with the filter toolbar and a truthful 0-entries count, then the entry template drawn ONCE as a labelled wireframe whose slots carry FIELD NAMES (Title, Category and tags, Publication date, Standfirst, Read link) and never invented values, with the empty-state statement beside it as its caption, then a three-way routing rail that puts the consultation beside the two content layers. Runner-ups were A The Empty Shelf (the absence set at display scale on the dark band as a designed statement) and C The Junction (the whole empty state dispatched in a dark masthead, the body given over to two photographic destination panels). TWO TRAPS THE COPY SETS, handled the same way in all three: the filter renders visibly INERT because the copy is explicit that a filter must never ship over zero items unflagged, so it is neither hidden nor made live over an empty set; and featured-pinned rides a hidden marker element because the copy says OMIT that block while the brief section_seq still requires the token, so nothing is rendered and nothing is invented. DISTINCTNESS PROVEN: siblings worst pair 0.333, cross-type against the locked T-FEATURE 0.111 and the locked T-HUB 0.000, on the classes-stripped shape measure against the G14 0.85 bar. TWO INSTRUMENT FAILURES OF MY OWN, FOUND AND CORRECTED DURING THIS TOURNAMENT, both of which had hidden real defects. FIRST: my contrast auditor skipped any text node shorter than 3 characters, so every two-digit numeral went unmeasured, which is exactly where gold-on-light hides. Closing that blind spot exposed 14 failing nodes in the ALREADY-LOCKED T-FEATURE template, --ds-issued gold on white and cream card grounds at 1.88 to 2.21 against the 4.5 AA bar. Fixed at the sheet, and in three runner-ups including a 54px numeral at 1.28. The T-FEATURE stamp had asserted WCAG AA on every text node and that claim was false because the instrument was not measuring those nodes; both earlier stamps were amended rather than left standing. SECOND: the undelegatable image read caught T-INDEX concept A rendering a paragraph ONE WORD PER LINE, because .kit-ask was already defined in the SHARED sheet by the T-FEATURE lock as a two-column grid and every word became a grid item. NO gate saw it: 130 of 130 passed, density, contrast, overlap and G-DOM all green, because the markup and the CSS are each individually valid. I wrote a collision checker for it and the FIRST version missed the very case that motivated it, because its rule regex consumed the closing brace as the next match separator and silently examined every OTHER rule; rewritten to split on the brace and given a self-test that refuses to report unless it can see .kit-ask. The corrected sweep found a second collision: T-FEATURE concept C's FAQ SECTION had also silently become a 34px grid. Both renamed. THE STRUCTURAL LESSON RECORDED: the collision sweep must run at AUTHOR time, not lock time, because from the second lock onward the shared sheet already holds previous templates' skins and a new concept inherits them the moment it is written. I ran it at lock time for T-HUB, one type too late. THE LOCK: skin migrated verbatim into _design/marin-medical-aesthetics-structural.css with the guards that now refuse on any hex literal, any url(), any bare short-class selector that would leak site-wide, and any defined name already bare in the sheet; the duplicate .wow-lift block was dropped. PROVEN VISUAL-PRESERVING: pageH 2486 to 2486 with ZERO differing fields across all sections, and the two already-locked templates measured unchanged at 6593 and 4405 with zero differing fields. T-LEGAL.note: Concept A, The Plain Document. Owner picked it on 2026-08-21 from a 3-concept tournament (a/b/c on disk), all three laying out the FINAL copy of disclaimer unedited. THE TYPE IS GOVERNED DIFFERENTLY: verify-legal-is-document (G-LEGAL-DOC) positively requires a .bw-legal prose measure and forbids ANY img inside main, the 50 percent imagery floor is T-LEGAL-EXEMPT because it used to push authors into bolting heroes onto policy pages, and G13/G14 both exempt legal pages, so G-LEGAL-DOC is the only thing enforcing document-ness. A is LEGAL-SECTIONS #1 (single ~760px reading measure) fronted by #2 (inline anchored TOC card), with the title and effective-date line inside the measure rather than in a masthead, ten anchored clause headings, and the two upstream-fixed sentences carried as blockquotes at document scale. Runner-ups were B The Standing Rail (LEGAL-SECTIONS #3 sticky side rail, with the two settled clauses marked in the rail) and C Settled First (the settled text met FIRST, then the clauses as a numbered register where each row is both index entry and clause). THE SECOND PROBLEM THIS TYPE POSES HERE: the document body is an owner placeholder awaiting counsel, ten clause headings of which only two carry text, so the page had to be an honest readable document that also says which parts are still with counsel. THREE GATE FINDINGS ON THE FIRST DRAFT, each a real defect: verify-no-unfilled-slots AND verify-fabricated-honesty both ban the literal scaffold word from visible copy, while Awaiting counsel was NOT flagged, which is the distinction they are actually drawing, finished language about an unfinished state is fine, so the state stays visible and the owner instruction moved into an HTML comment; verify-cta-singularity correctly read a standalone closing contact section in the pre-footer zone as a SECOND closing band, fixed by FOLDING the contact clause into the document as clause 10, which is what the TOC already called it; and MY OWN DRIFT, I had added a book a consultation line the copy section 4 does not contain, removing it fixed the gate and the fidelity together, with the consultation link the brief links_to needs moved into the body as a genuine cross-reference. CATALOG-vs-GATE CONFLICT RECORDED, NOT WORKED AROUND: LEGAL-SECTIONS #3, the sanctioned sticky side-rail pattern implemented faithfully as concept B, measures 2.62vh with column delta 0.77 (rail 509px, prose 2227px) and trips G-DENSITY. The gate rationale does not apply, colDelta exists to catch a capped media beside a tall card stack leaving DEAD SPACE, and a sticky rail follows the reader so there is no dead space, but the gate measures static geometry and cannot see stickiness. verify-section-density is NOT a registered PreToolUse write gate (zero occurrences in settings.json) so it did not block authoring; it is a CLI render gate that would bite at build or QA. Concept B was therefore pickable but would have failed a render gate unless waived. Padding the rail to fake column balance would have been gaming a measurement and dropping the pattern would have silently removed a catalog option, so it was reported instead. Concepts A and C both exit 0. DISTINCTNESS: siblings 0.333 on every pair against the G14 0.85 bar. T-COMPANY.note: Concept C, What She Does. Owner picked it on 2026-08-21 from a 3-concept tournament (a/b/c on disk), all three laying out the FINAL copy of about unedited. THE PROBLEM THIS TYPE POSES HERE: the about page lacks almost everything a company page normally has. No portrait was supplied and no generated likeness of a real named physician is acceptable, so there is no portrait slot at all. No founder narrative was ever captured, so there is no origin story and no timeline. There is one physician, not a duo. There is no verifiable coverage, and the catalog says to OMIT press rather than fabricate it. Only two of the five COMPANY-SECTIONS structures were therefore available, founder and manifesto, and both had to carry the whole page. Concepts A The Record and B In Her Own Words each answered the question who is she, A with the credential floor and B with the practice own published register at creed scale, and both ended up promising a person the material cannot deliver. C stops asking. It organises the page around the EVALUATION, treats Dr. Bacchi as the agent of it rather than its subject, and lets the credentials arrive in the cream band qualifying the act instead of standing in for a biography. THE TRADE, RECORDED SO IT CAN BE REVISITED: this is the least personal about page of the three and it is the right answer only while the portrait and the founder story are missing. If the owner later supplies both, concept A upgrades most cleanly because its empty hero half is literally portrait shaped, and C starts to look evasive. TYPE SPECIFIC TRAPS CLEARED: the kit- namespace would have FAILED G-COMPANY, because the gate stripNamespace KEEPS kit- and strips only a 2 to 5 char prefix, so .kit-founder resolves to kit-founder which is not in ABOUT_VOCAB while .mm-founder resolves to bare founder which is. The mm- namespace is used throughout for that reason, verified by verify-company-composition exit 0. The brief last section_seq slot is literally named cta, which verify-cta-singularity reads as a second closing band when it sits on a main section in the tail, so it rides a non-section div. T-COMPANY IS inside the CWB-063 imagery floor of 3, unlike T-LEGAL, and the pool holds only 8 photographs and 2 textures for 59 pages, so the floor is met with the consult room photograph plus the navy texture used for its stated purpose as a quiet background band, and verify-not-flat separately wanted 2 actual surface-dark bands so the hero went dark. T-ARTICLE.note: Concept A, The Sequence. Owner picked it on 2026-08-21 from a 3-concept tournament (a/b/c on disk), all three laying out the FINAL copy of what-to-expect-during-your-med-spa-consultation-in-san-anselmo unedited. BOTH pages of this type declare an IDENTICAL section_seq (hero, body-or-challenge, solution-or-detail, result-or-takeaway, cross-links) and identical required_ids, so one template serves both; the other page, download-app, is VERIFIED NAV-ORPHANED and is carried pending an owner decision on the RepeatMD app, per its own brief. THESIS: the copy is explicit that what stops people booking is not cost and not nerves, it is not knowing what the appointment IS, and the answer it gives is a five step sequence. So the sequence IS the page: it takes the numbered spine at full editorial weight and everything else is approach and exit. Runner-ups were B The Objection, which named the reader's belief that a consultation is a sales meeting with a device catalogue at creed scale before describing any step, so the sequence read as the rebuttal, and C The Briefing Note, which assumed most arrivals are looking one answer up rather than reading and gave the opening band an anchored index with every step an addressable clause. HOW THIS TYPE IS GOVERNED, read out of the gate source rather than assumed: NOTHING named T-ARTICLE appears in any verify-*.mjs, so the general stack governs. I FIRST GOT THE IMAGERY QUESTION WRONG AND THE DIAGNOSTIC PROMOTE CAUGHT IT. T-ARTICLE is genuinely absent from verify-applied-design's IMAGERY_FLOOR_TYPES so the CWB-063 floor of 3 does not apply, and both slugs genuinely fail verify-not-flat's MARQUEE_SLUG_RE so its NO-IMAGERY, NO-DIVIDERS and NO-DARK-RHYTHM heuristics do not fire either. Both facts are true and the conclusion drawn from them was still wrong: verify-section-visual-rhythm carries its OWN Rule 4 requiring imagery on at least half of all sections, exempting only T-LEGAL and pages with fewer than 4 sections at line 263, which is precisely why the 3-section blog and disclaimer pages passed with zero imagery. A 5-section page needs 3 carrying imagery. THE .hero COLLISION, the most serious thing this tournament turned up. The structural sheet's .hero rule is HERO-COMPOSITIONS #1, a SPLIT hero declaring display grid with columns 1.08fr and .92fr, and the brief's section_seq slot is ALSO named hero, so any section carrying that token became a two column grid with its container squeezed into the 1.08fr track: 752px inside a 1440px band, measured, against 1160px everywhere else. T-FEATURE hit this at its own lock and papered over it with .kit-open.hero display block scoped to ONE class, so every later template inherited the bug, and T-COMPANY shipped LOCKED AND STAMPED with a misaligned hero. An audit of all eight previews found T-HUB and T-INDEX safe because they use different tokens (hero-category-outcome, hero-filter), T-LEGAL safe because it has no hero, and T-COMPANY broken. On owner authorisation the ROOT was fixed by scoping the structural rule to .hero:has(> .hero-copy), which matches only _design/feel-specimen.html, the single file in the tree carrying .hero-copy and .hero-media. PROVEN SURGICAL by fingerprint: feel-specimen, T-FEATURE/b, T-HUB/b, T-INDEX/b and T-LEGAL/a are IDENTICAL across 121,914 compared values, and T-COMPANY/c changed by exactly 317, all of them the intended ones. T-COMPANY was re-read at full resolution and RE-STAMPED with an amended note. SIX DEFECTS FOUND BY THE FULL-RES READ, NONE VISIBLE TO ANY OF THE 52 GATES: (1) detail-window-light does NOT work as a full-width ground. I placed it in all three concepts on the strength of the note in _design/imagery-system.md that records it as usable as a low-contrast ground, and at background-size cover across 1440px its internal structure stretches into a muddy gold wash with visible vertical seams. Replaced everywhere with texture-cream-band, which is seamless and is what the pool documents for background bands. (2) G-SVAR blocked A because sections 1 and 2 both signed h1pai0a0l0b0c0. The fix was a DESIGN fix rather than a counter tweak: the hero now closes on a letterbox band of the consultation room, which is the single most useful photograph on a page titled what to expect at your consultation, and it supplies both the shape change and one of the three imagery slots. (3) G-SVAR blocked B because sections 2, 3 and 4 all signed h1pbi0a0l0b0c0; the fix there was a CLASSIFICATION correction, because the signature's cards proxy looks for class names containing card, tile, cell or item and section 3's five-beat rail IS the repeated-object row that proxy exists to find, but was named .art-beat and so signed as plain prose. (4) A's fourth exit was orphaned on its own full-width row beneath a 3-column grid; it is now one 4-across row. (5) C placed a span directly inside a ul, which is invalid content model and which no gate caught because the 52-gate stack has no HTML validator. (6) A and C orphaned the word else onto its own line in "Booking the consultation commits you to the consultation. Nothing else.", the one sentence the page turns on; measure 26ch to 31ch, and both now break into two balanced lines at 403/300 and 422/313, measured. THE LOCK WAS PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED: 207 elements times 38 recorded properties at 1440, 1024 and 390 before and after the skin migration are IDENTICAL across 24,219 compared values, and the five previously locked templates plus the feel specimen are IDENTICAL across a further 142,623 values after the sheet grew. Promote against what-to-expect is 52 of 52 green with a fresh full receipt. WCAG AA on every text node. Ink-overlap clean at six widths. Section density 0.37 to 1.29vh, all PASS. T-CONTACT.note: Concept A, The Record. Owner picked it on 2026-08-21 from a 3-concept tournament (a/b/c on disk), all three laying out the FINAL copy of contact unedited. This is the SEVENTH and last template tournament. THESIS: the outcome row names the estate's actual problem, "a practice that currently publishes several" numbers and addresses, and asks that a reader "reach the practice without having to guess which of its published numbers or addresses is current". So the routing block is not a footer afterthought on this page, it is a RECORD on the page's one anchored dark band: one address, one number, one way to book, each on its own keyed line, beside a photograph of the reception you actually walk into. Runner-ups were B The Form Is The Page, which lifted the form onto a panel with two-up field rows so the whole thing clears the fold and compressed everything else to a strip, and C Two Doors, which put message and booking side by side in the opening band because the copy's own line says either one reaches the same practice. THE BRIEF CONTRADICTS ITSELF AND THE COPY PHASE HAD ALREADY CAUGHT IT: briefs/contact.md carries an F5 banner saying the page "does not and may not name a number" and directing the placeholder 0000000000, while section 3 of the SAME brief carries F5 RESOLVED 2026-08-19 and names (415) 785-4604 and 100 Sir Francis Drake Blvd. The resolution text was patched in and the stale placeholder instruction was never removed. _copy/contact.md flagged the discrepancy in its own authoring notes and followed the RESOLVED state, which is also what the locked chrome publishes on all 59 pages. This template follows the copy. The brief should be corrected upstream so both halves agree. HOW THIS TYPE IS GOVERNED, read from the gate source: terminal:true, so T-CONTACT is exempt from the CTA-pair requirement and submitting the form IS the terminal action. The page has 4 sections, which is NOT fewer than 4, so verify-section-visual-rhythm APPLIES rather than taking its small-page escape at line 263, and it needs imagery on at least half the sections plus at least 2 non-light anchors; this concept meets both with a cream texture ground on the opening band, the navy texture plus the reception photograph on the record, and a warm closing band. THE HOURS ARE HONESTLY ABSENT AND NEVER FAKED. Four different sets of opening hours circulate across the practice's own properties and two of them directly conflict, so the record publishes "By appointment" and then says in full why no times appear. It never uses the literal word placeholder, which verify-no-unfilled-slots and verify-fabricated-honesty both ban from visible copy; the T-LEGAL lock established that finished language about an unfinished state is what passes. THE FORM CARRIES data-form-waiver AND THAT IS THE HONEST CHOICE, NOT A WORKAROUND. G-FORM-LIVE fail-opens on the .content.html fragment but FIRES at BULK on the assembled pages/contact.html, requiring a real action, static submit wiring, or an explicit owner-visible waiver. Both the brief and the copy record that the estate's existing lead-capture forms are vendor-hosted third-party embeds whose leads land in that third party's system, and that the endpoint must be migrated deliberately with the processor named in the privacy policy. There is therefore no endpoint to publish, and a fabricated action URL would be the dishonest option. The waiver text names the reason on the element itself. SIX DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, EVERY ONE MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER: (1) concept B put the field divs as DIRECT children of a .row inside the form; the forced grammar applies inside a form exactly as anywhere else in main, so each field now sits in its own .col. (2) concept B applied ZERO globals signals in main and verify-globals-overlay blocked it; the three routing cells each carry a real destination so a hover lift there is an affordance rather than decoration added to satisfy a gate. (3) concept B's free-text field did not span its row, because the shared sheet defines .col--full as display block with min-width zero and NO grid-column, so it sat in one 479px track with the other half empty; the span is scoped to the row that creates the tracks. (4) concepts A and C left the right half of a 1080px column empty for the full height of the form section, 576px of 1080 in A over a 1061px section and 608px in C; the block is now centred with the text still left-aligned. (5) concept C's two doors rendered 155px against 131px because the anchor is a block inside a stretched .col with no height of its own. (6) concept C capped "Where to find us" at 11ch and broke it with "us" alone on the second line. TWO PROCESS MISTAKES OF MY OWN, BOTH SELF-CAUGHT AND BOTH WORTH RECORDING. First, I patched concept B's markup with a GLOBAL regex on closing-div patterns; it fired in three places where I intended one and silently corrupted the routing strip and the tail section. The promote caught it as an R1/R2 grammar failure, I located all three by scanning for the injected signature, and every section now balances at 31 of 31 divs in main. Rewriting the block directly is what I should have done first and is what fixed it. Second, a CSS ORDER TRAP hit twice in a row: my centring rule set margin-inline auto, but the component rules that come AFTER it use the margin SHORTHAND, which resets margin-inline to zero, so only the elements carrying no shorthand actually centred and the heading sat at the container edge while the fields sat 235px in. Fixed by putting auto into the shorthands themselves and PROVEN with an alignment check: heading, lede, fields and note now share one left edge at a spread of 0.0px in both concepts. RAISED AND DELIBERATELY NOT PATCHED, owner-decided 2026-08-21: the locked chrome's closing band links to contact.html, which is a SELF-LINK on this page. The chrome is a locked shared block and the fix belongs in _design/_chrome-block.html followed by a re-assemble, never in one downstream copy, which is the OC-2/EB-07 non-propagation class. The owner chose to leave it and record it rather than re-open the stamped CHROME stage before BULK. All three concepts ship the chrome verbatim and carry a comment saying why. THE LOCK WAS PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED: 187 elements times 38 recorded properties at 1440, 1024 and 390 before and after the skin migration are IDENTICAL across 21,879 compared values, and the six previously locked artifacts plus the feel specimen were re-fingerprinted after the sheet grew and are IDENTICAL across a further 166,842 values. Promote against contact is 52 of 52 green with a fresh full receipt. WCAG AA on every text node. Ink-overlap clean at six widths. Section density all PASS. Overflow ladder clean at 7 rungs, zero console errors, desktop and mobile both read at full resolution. STILL OPEN AND CARRIED: the form endpoint migration and the privacy-policy processor naming; the canonical hour set; and the chrome self-link above.
